readerTitle: Why a 10% fee can take half a seller's profit
caseNote: 가상 사례 (대형 인테리어 소매 체인 안의 설치기사 마켓플레이스 팀, 프리랜서 디자인 플랫폼) + 앱스토어 수수료에 대한 일반적 언급 · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 수수료율은 거래 금액이 아니라 판매자가 한 건에서 남기는 이익에 대어 보아야 한다. 그리고 그 상한은 플랫폼이 그 거래에 더해 주는 가치다.
misconception: 10%는 작은 수수료다. 수수료율을 두 배로 올리면 매출도 두 배가 된다.

sources.text: 마켓플레이스 지표의 표준 개념 (take rate = 플랫폼 매출 ÷ 총거래액 GMV)
Apple App Store Review Guidelines 및 App Store Small Business Program 발표 (2020)
설치기사·디자인 플랫폼의 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 설치 작업 계산: 작업가 $1,000, 기사 비용 $800, 수수료 전 이익 $200. 수수료 10% = $100, 기사 몫 $100. 수수료 20% = $200, 기사 몫 $0. 수수료 10%는 기사 이익의 50%.
팀 매출: 월 거래액 $2M × 10% = $200k. 20%로 올리고 거래량이 그대로라면 $400k, 실제로는 기사 이탈로 거래량이 줄 수 있음.
차트 계산: 수수료 10%가 판매자 이익에서 차지하는 비율 = 10% ÷ 판매자 이익률. 이익률 20% → 50%, 10% → 100%, 80% → 12.5%. 모두 가상 이익률입니다.
앱스토어가 디지털 판매에 최대 30%를 받아 왔다는 점은 일반적으로 알려진 사실이며, Apple이 소규모 개발자에게 15%를 적용하는 프로그램을 2020년에 발표했습니다. 게시 전 Apple 공식 자료와 이후 규정 변경(지역별 규제 포함)을 다시 확인하세요.

cards.title: The fee went up 10 points. The installer's profit went to zero.
body: A platform charges installers 10% of every job. Someone suggests 20%. It sounds like a small tweak.
For an installer earning $200 on a $1,000 job, it's not small at all. It's everything.

image.label: An installer's toolbox with a coin being lifted out by a hand
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 설치기사의 공구함 위에 동전 두 개. 위에서 내려온 손이 동전 두 개를 모두 집어 가는 장면. 상단에 "10% → 20%" 라벨. 실제 기업 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Leadership wants double the revenue.
body: You run the installer marketplace team inside a big home-improvement chain. Customers book independent installers on the chain's website. Jobs total $2M a month, and your 10% fee brings in $200k.
Leadership wants $400k and suggests a 20% fee. Which number do you check first?

options.feedback: Useful context, but rivals have different services and sellers. It tells you what's common, not what your installers can bear.

options.text: How much an installer keeps per job after their own costs
options.feedback: This shows how much of their profit you already take. It's the number that decides whether they stay.

options.text: Revenue at 20% if job volume stays the same
options.feedback: It gives the $400k leadership wants, on paper. But it assumes installers won't raise prices, leave or take jobs elsewhere.

cards.title: Follow one $1,000 job.
body: At 10%, you take **half** the installer's profit. At 20%, you take all of it. The fee doubled. Their take-home fell from $100 to $0.

cards.title: Take rate
body: A **take rate** is the share of each transaction a marketplace keeps as its own revenue. It's your revenue divided by the total value of deals on your platform, often called *gross merchandise value* or GMV.
The buyer sees the price. The seller feels the fee against what they keep. That's why a modest-sounding rate can feel huge.

image.label: A $1,000 bar with a 10% slice cut from a thin profit layer
image.brief: 가로 막대 하나가 $1,000. 대부분은 회색 "Seller's costs $800", 끝의 얇은 초록 층이 "Profit $200". 10% 수수료 조각이 그 초록 층의 절반을 잘라 가는 모습.

cards.title: A take rate has a floor and a ceiling.
body: Sellers don't compare your fee to zero. They compare it to finding customers on their own.
list: **Floor:** what it costs you to run each deal, like payments, support and marketing
**Ceiling:** the value you add, like customers they couldn't reach, trust, scheduling and getting paid on time
**Seller margin:** the thinner it is, the less room under the ceiling
cards.callout: To raise the rate, raise the value you add first.
cards.softwareNote: App stores have long taken up to 30% on digital sales, and Apple later cut this to 15% for smaller developers. Digital goods cost little to make again, so sellers have more profit for a fee to come from.

cards.title: A 10% fee as a share of the seller's profit
body: The same 10% rate means very different things to different sellers. A thin-margin seller hands over most of their profit.

groups.label: Share of seller profit taken by a 10% fee

cards.title: Lower isn't always better either.
body: A rate too low can't pay for the things that make the marketplace worth using: vetting sellers, handling disputes, bringing in buyers.
Rates are also hard to raise later. Sellers built their prices around the old one, and some will start arranging repeat deals off your platform.
And compare rates carefully. Some platforms also charge buyers a fee, so the headline seller rate isn't the whole take.

cards.title: Now it's a freelance design app.
body: Your app matches small businesses with freelance designers and takes 5%. You need more revenue. Many designers find a client through you, then keep working with them for months.

options.feedback: Simple and quick revenue. But designers with long-term clients may feel you charge more for work you no longer help with, and move it off the app.

options.text: Charge more on a new client's first jobs, less on repeat work
options.feedback: The fee follows the value: high when you brought the client, low when the relationship runs itself. You earn less on repeat work but keep it on the app.

options.text: Keep 5% and add a monthly subscription for designers
options.feedback: It adds steady revenue without touching the rate. But designers who rarely win work may pay for nothing and leave.

cards.title: Measure your fee against what the seller keeps.
body: A take rate isn't small or large on its own. It's small or large next to the seller's profit and the value you add to each deal.
**Try it today:** pick one supplier or partner you pay a commission to, or who pays one to you. Work out what share of their profit that fee really is.
